items.title: Stocks in news: Biocon, Bank of Baroda, TCS, Sanofi India and Tata Capital
items.description: Indian equity markets hit a seven-week low on Tuesday, primarily due to escalating crude oil prices and geopolitical instability that swayed investor morale. Notably, Bank of Baroda announced plans to divest its interest in the NSE, while TCS secured a major contract. Other companies such as Sanofi India and Piramal Finance also shared pivotal developments, highlighting a mixed bag of corporate activity.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Indian stock markets wrapped up on Tuesday near their crisis points, strained by high Brent crude oil prices and geopolitical instability that dampened investor morale. Market analysts warn of an ongoing downward trend, calling for stronger highs and lows to initiate a turnaround. Despite foreign portfolio investors offloading shares, domestic institutional players capitalized as net buyers.

items.title: These 6 banking stocks have an upside potential of up to 25% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: At a time when a statement or missile can cause unexplained volatility, expecting rational behaviour in the equity markets is probably expecting too much. But the fact is that rationality finally prevails. And it has to do with earnings and fundamentals and macro-economic order. Check out Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, for price targets of over 4,000 listed stocks along with detailed company analysis focusing on five key components ,earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum, to generate standardised scores. SR Plus Reports is a complimentary offering to ETPrime members.

items.title: FPIs sell $1.6 billion of Indian stocks in five trading sessions
items.description: After a brief period of optimism, foreign investors are retreating from Indian stocks as rising crude oil prices and escalating global bond yields shift market dynamics. This change reflects a waning interest in emerging market growth assets, compounded by profit-taking strategies and a pivot towards AI investments. While domestic buying could offer some support, ongoing external pressures may dampen overall returns.

items.title: Defence stocks rally as DAC clears Rs 1.10 lakh crore acquisition proposals
items.description: Defence stocks experienced a notable surge on Tuesday following government approval for military acquisitions. These proposals, valued at approximately ₹1.10 lakh crore, will largely benefit domestic manufacturers. The Nifty India Defence index reached a record high, reflecting strong investor confidence in the sector. Analysts highlight the significant order inflow visibility and structural growth opportunities for Indian companies.

items.title: BSE shares fall 4% to snap 3-day rally as Bernstein forecasts up to 17% downside
items.description: BSE shares fell sharply on Wednesday after Bernstein initiated coverage with an Underperform rating and a Rs 2,820 target, implying 17% downside. The brokerage expects retail participation in equity derivatives to moderate and BSE’s market share gains to peak in FY27. Meanwhile, CAS-related volume concerns add to the pressure.

items.title: Trump strikes Indian IT again! Why tech stocks lost Rs 55,000 crore in a single session
items.description: Indian IT stocks lost around Rs 55,000 crore in market value after the US suspended Cognizant’s PERM labour certification filings, raising fresh concerns over tighter scrutiny of work visas and alleged visa fraud.

items.title: ​6 superstar investors, 6 big bets of Madhusudan Kela, Ashish Kacholia & others
items.description: Investors keenly watch out for market moves made by ace investors which mostly prove to beat the overall stock market volatility. Here are the top stock holdings of ace investors Radhakishan Damani, Ashish Kacholia, Madhusudan Kela, Vijay Kedia, Mukul Agrawal and Dolly Khanna.

items.title: $60 billion opportunity! Will defence stocks fire on all cylinders and who will be the biggest beneficiary?
items.description: India’s defence sector is entering a new growth phase, with the combat use of indigenous weapons boosting the credibility and export potential of locally developed systems. Defence spending has risen sharply from Rs 2.53 trillion in FY14 to Rs 6.81 trillion in FY26, while the government’s Atmanirbhar Bharat push is creating long-term opportunities.

items.title: Invesco’s ₹16,000 crore midcap fund delivered 426% return in 10 years. Aditya Khemani reveals the strategy
items.description: Invesco India Midcap Fund has impressively delivered a 426% return over a decade, showcasing an investment strategy that values robust earnings potential and strong management teams. The fund employs a concentrated portfolio approach with a moderate turnover rate, aiming to compound earnings over three to five years. This blend of growth and value investing fosters ongoing value creation for its investors.

items.title: Biocon shares rise 3% after Rs 638-crore block deal; Active Pine likely seller
items.description: Biocon shares rose after a block deal involving around 1.65 crore shares. Investor Active Pine was reportedly looking to sell up to 1.66 crore shares, or about 1% stake, for around Rs 638 crore at a floor price of Rs 385 per share, implying a discount of up to 1.9% to the market price. The seller will face a 30-day lock-up on further stake sales.

items.title: Why stock market is down today? Sensex plunges 600 points, Nifty below 23,500. 6 key triggers behind D-Street selloff
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced significant losses as Sensex and Nifty declined. Soaring oil prices and other factors spooked investors, leading to a market downturn. Major IT stocks like Infosys and TCS saw considerable drops, impacting the overall market. Broader markets also followed the downward trend, with midcap and smallcap indices falling. The total market capitalization saw a substantial reduction of approximately two lakh crore rupees.

items.title: Largecap safety trade? 8 Nifty stocks test investor patience with losses for two years
items.description: Over the past two years, eight Nifty stocks have experienced declines, with notable IT giants like TCS and Infosys pressured by shifts in client spending patterns. Additionally, Tata Motors faced a dip due to difficulties at Jaguar Land Rover, while valuation worries plagued Trent, alongside ITC's tax complications. Nevertheless, a faction of fund managers remains optimistic about large-cap stocks, indicating a mixed outlook for investors.

items.title: Jefferies picks 5 defence stocks with upside potential of up to 39% after DAC’s Rs 1.1 lakh crore proposal
items.description: India’s defence industry is entering a higher growth phase as combat deployment of indigenous weapons during Operation Sindoor strengthens the credibility of locally made systems in global markets. Jefferies expects defence exports to rise 11% annually through fiscal 2030, reaching Rs 584 billion, and has identified 5 stocks that can potentially perform well in the coming quarters.

items.title: Nifty’s next rally needs two battered warhorses to wake up. Which one will revive first?
items.description: For a continued uptrend, India's Nifty index relies heavily on the resurgence of the banking and IT sectors. Banks are poised for a quicker recovery owing to factors like enhanced liquidity and credit growth. Meanwhile, while IT firms navigate the complexities posed by AI, they still present attractive valuation opportunities for selective investments. Foreign investor activity remains pivotal in determining market trends, with small and mid-cap stocks currently gaining traction.

items.title: Coforge shares crash 9% after Chairman Om Prakash Bhatt resigns post audit
items.description: Coforge shares fell after Chairperson Om Prakash Bhatt resigned. An internal audit identified concerns regarding the board evaluation process and its presentation. Bhatt stated his resignation was appropriate given the circumstances and disagreements. The company clarified his departure followed audit findings and board discussions. Coforge reported strong financial results in its first quarter.

items.title: JPMorgan, Jane Street probes show India scrutinizing Wall Street
items.description: India’s market regulator Sebi is intensifying scrutiny of global financial firms, targeting entities linked to JPMorgan, Jane Street, Bank of America and Capital Group over alleged market misconduct. The crackdown focuses on protecting retail investors, particularly in India’s huge options market, while pushing foreign institutions to strengthen compliance as regulatory oversight becomes more stringent.

items.title: Adani Airports to raise Rs 9,825 crore from Temasek, BlackRock, Premji Invest and Alpha Wave
items.description: Adani Enterprises will raise around $1 billion by issuing fresh shares in its airport unit, Adani Airport Holdings, to investors including Temasek, BlackRock, Premji Invest and Alpha Wave. The transaction will result in the consortium holding up to 5.54% in the business, while Adani Enterprises will retain control. The fresh capital will be used to fund the airport business.

items.title: PVR Inox among 5 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On September 8, five stocks in the Nifty500 pack were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge. An uptrend signal occurs when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" means that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are increasing, indicating strengthening momentum in the stock's price. The RSI is a technical indicator commonly used by traders to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: Finolex Cables among 4 Nifty500 stocks flashing bullish signals
items.description: On September 8, four Nifty500 stocks appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in which the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level towards the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on September 8, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: CLSA sees 29% downside in Meesho despite a 19% YTD rally. Buy, sell or hold?
items.description: CLSA maintained an Underperform rating on Meesho with a Rs 150 target, citing stretched valuations and optimism around advertising monetisation, order frequency and logistics savings. The brokerage sees significant downside if these growth drivers fail to meet market expectations.

items.title: How Apple shares may react to the launch of first-ever foldable iPhone? Here’s what analysts say
items.description: Apple’s first-ever foldable iPhone could significantly impact the company’s growth and stock performance. Analysts expect the device, potentially priced at $2,000-$2,500, to generate over $45 billion in revenue by the end of next year. Apple shares have historically gained after iPhone launches, while investors will closely track foldable demand, pricing and AI features.

items.title: Multibagger Stocks: 14 microcaps surged up to 355% in just 6 months
items.description: Despite weakness across the broader market, India’s microcap segment has delivered exceptional returns over the past six months. While the benchmark Nifty 50 fell nearly 3%, the Nifty Microcap 250 index climbed around 31%, significantly outperforming the frontline index.The rally has been broad-based, with nearly 60 microcap stocks gaining more than 50% during the period. Among them, 14 stocks surged between 100% and 355%, more than doubling investors’ wealth in just six months and highlighting strong momentum and rising investor interest in the segment. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Thinking long term and enduring volatility is the only way out: 5 mid-caps from different sectors with upside potential of up to 24%
items.description: If you are an investor with some skin in the game, be ready to see some underperformance. Why? Because valuation readjustment can take more time in a volatile market. Buying a good business in a correction does not mean its price stops falling the day you buy. It can drift lower, or go nowhere, for a while, as the market takes its time to settle. That is the nature of a volatile phase, and why it is an exercise in patience.

items.title: Beyond the runway: Emkay sees up to 25% upside in GMR Airports
items.description: Emkay Global has initiated coverage on GMR Airports with a Buy rating and a Rs 120 target price, implying 25% upside from the current levels. The brokerage expects non-aeronautical and adjacent businesses such as duty-free, cargo and airport-linked developments to drive incremental profitability, while stronger earnings and cash flows support margin expansion and deleveraging through FY29.

items.title: India’s textile boom ahead? Why Jefferies is bullish on Welspun, Raymond
items.description: Jefferies upgraded Welspun Living to Buy and more than doubled its target to Rs 260, while initiating coverage on Raymond Lifestyle with a Rs 900 target. The brokerage expects FTAs, China+1 sourcing and improving export competitiveness to drive multi-year growth.

items.title: ASM Tech shares rally 10% to record high as Radhakishan Damani, Mukul Agrawal join Rs 526-crore preferential issue
items.description: ASM Technologies share price rallied sharply on Wednesday to hit a record high after the company approved a Rs 526-crore preferential issue involving entities linked to Radhakishan Damani and Mukul Agrawal. The engineering services firm will issue 10.78 lakh shares at Rs 4,875 apiece, while existing investors will gain fresh exposure.

items.title: Paytm shares jump 5% as workplace AI push gains traction
items.description: Paytm shares surged on Wednesday, as investors welcomed the company’s push into enterprise AI, marking an expansion beyond its core payments business. The stock has gained over 20% in the past month, significantly outperforming the broader Nifty 500 and Nifty 50.

items.title: Sterlite Tech shares jump 5% to fresh 52-week high, multibagger skyrockets 745% in 2026. What lies ahead?
items.description: Sterlite Technologies shares hit a fresh 52-week high after rising 5% to the upper circuit, taking their 2026 gains to 745%. The rally follows the company’s growth plans, capacity expansion and strong Q1 performance, supported by robust demand for optical connectivity products.

items.title: IFCI shares fall 4% on reports of lower price band for NSE IPO
items.description: IFCI shares fell sharply on Wednesday after reports suggested NSE could price its IPO below earlier indications and reduce the stake offered. The proposed price band of Rs 1,700–1,785 values NSE at around Rs 4.4 lakh crore. IFCI’s indirect exposure to NSE through Stock Holding Corporation has put its shares under pressure.

items.title: PC Jeweller shares jump 4%, surge 38% in one week. What's polishing the stock's shine?
items.description: PC Jeweller shares have surged 38% in a week and 40% in a month as the company moves closer to becoming debt-free. The jeweller has repaid outstanding dues to 10 of 14 consortium banks and cleared more than 96% of the remaining debt.

items.title: Graphite India shares rocket over 18% to extend gains for second session. What’s behind the surge?
items.description: Graphite India shares surged 18.5% after GrafTech announced a minimum 30% hike in graphite electrode prices, raising hopes of improved realisations and margins. The company’s June-quarter profit rose 28.4%, while EBITDA margin expanded sharply to 17.1%.

items.title: Adani Enterprises shares gain over 4% as airports arm plans to raise $1 billion from Temasek, BlackRock, others
items.description: Adani Enterprises shares rose over 4% after Adani Airport Holdings announced a Rs 9,825-crore equity raise from Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and BlackRock-managed funds. The funds will support airport expansion, modernisation and Airport City projects. AAHL expects the investment to boost capacity, while Adani Enterprises continues delivering strong share-price gains.

items.title: ESDS Software shares rally 10%, skyrocket 235% from IPO price in 4 days. Should you buy or sell?
items.description: ESDS Software share price has surged 235% from its IPO price in just four sessions, with the stock hitting the upper circuit in every session since listing. While analysts remain positive on the company’s long-term growth prospects, they flag elevated valuations and execution risks.

items.title: Nifty drops 4% in less than 5 weeks despite attractive valuations in largecaps. What can reverse this trend?
items.description: Despite their appealing valuations, Indian largecap stocks are currently on a downward trend. Meanwhile, the mid and smallcap sectors are enjoying consistent monthly SIP inflows. Analysts predict that a trend reversal for largecaps is on the horizon, spurred by upcoming mega IPOs from NSE and Jio. Investors are encouraged to prioritize largecap stocks with robust earnings visibility.

items.title: Sebi revises rules for open interest violations in commodity derivatives
items.description: Sebi has revised commodity derivatives position limits and penalties, effective immediately. The new framework caps violation charges, strengthens action against repeated breaches, and updates agri commodity classifications and limits, aiming to ease compliance while improving market risk management across exchanges.

items.title: India lifts ban on JPMorgan unit in index manipulation charge
items.description: India lifted its trading ban on JPMorgan unit Copthall Mauritius and Mansi Share after they deposited Rs 2.96 crore ($311,230) in alleged unlawful gains. Accused by SEBI of manipulating BSE Sensex closing auction prices to boost options bets, both entities can trade again while the investigation continues

items.title: Vodafone Idea among 4 stocks that hit 52-week highs & rallied up to 22% in a month
items.description: On Wednesday, the benchmark Sensex declined 813 points to close at 74,764. Despite the market weakness, four stocks from the BSE 150 Midcap index touched fresh 52-week highs, marking their highest levels in the past year. A 52-week high simply means that a stock has reached its highest price level over the past year and may indicate increased market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Vodafone Idea a high-beta turnaround play, says Jefferies; initiates buy with 29% upside potential
items.description: Jefferies initiated coverage on Vodafone Idea with a Buy rating and Rs 20 target, citing subscriber stabilisation, tariff hikes and operating leverage. The brokerage expects strong revenue and cash EBITDA growth, but flags funding needs, execution risks and cash outflows.

items.title: Sebi fines two Jindal Steel designated persons for trading-window violations
items.description: Sebi has fined two designated persons of Jindal Steel & Power Rs 1 lakh each for trading in the company’s shares and stock options during the trading-window closure period. The regulator also found that they executed trades above the prescribed threshold without obtaining pre-clearance, in violation of the company’s insider trading code.

items.title: Sebi proposes wider pool of MII board candidates, SOP for key officials
items.description: Sebi has proposed governance reforms for market infrastructure institutions, including relaxed director eligibility rules and standardised requirements for four key management roles. The proposals aim to widen access to expertise while strengthening technology, cybersecurity, compliance and risk management across MIIs.

items.title: MCX, IAMAI sign MoU to bring fintech solutions to commodity markets
items.description: MCX and IAMAI have signed an MoU to set up a Commodity Markets Innovation Council aimed at driving fintech-led innovation in India’s commodity markets. The industry-led platform will bring together stakeholders, startups and technology players to identify challenges, develop digital solutions, improve market access and support wider participation and efficiency.

items.title: Explained: Why Bernstein prefers MCX over BSE as volumes plummet amid CAS chaos
items.description: Bernstein has favoured MCX over BSE as commodity derivatives volumes maintain strong momentum while equity derivatives activity weakens amid the Closing Auction Session. The brokerage expects MCX’s growth to support earnings upgrades, while BSE faces moderating volumes, slowing market share gains and a sharp deceleration in earnings growth over the coming years.

items.title: Market wrap: Adani Ent, Max Healthcare, Infosys, HDFC Life among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Wednesday
items.description: Indian equities extended losses on September 9 as rising oil prices pressured sentiment. Sensex fell 813 points and Nifty declined 204 points. IT stocks led sectoral losses, while metals gained. Technical indicators remained bearish, though oversold conditions could trigger a rebound.

items.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit:  Decoding the next market cycle and where  opportunities lie
items.description: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0 will feature veteran investor Prashant Jain decoding the next market cycle and the opportunities it could present. Drawing on his decades of market experience, Jain will discuss navigating downturns and recoveries, assessing businesses and valuations, and managing risk as market conditions and investment themes evolve.

items.title: CAS Chaos Explained: What’s Driving The Final 20-Minute Volatility?
items.description: Why was CAS introduced in the first place & why has it made the final 20 minutes so volatile?From massive Sensex swings to SEBI scrutiny, we break down how the closing auction works, what’s going wrong, and what traders should watch next.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
items.description: Indian markets extended their losing streak for a third day as soaring oil prices and Middle East tensions hurt sentiment. Sensex fell 813 points, Nifty dropped 204 points, and BSE market capitalisation lost over Rs 2 lakh crore amid broad-based selling.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A power equipment maker for a 6.9% upmove, a large-cap thermal power stock for a gain of about 7%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: ICICI Prudential AMC gets RBI approval to buy up to 9.95% stake in Kotak and 3 other banks
items.description: ICICI Prudential AMC secured Reserve Bank of India approval for significant bank share acquisitions.  The approval allows for aggregate holdings up to 9.95 percent in four specific banks.  These banks include Kotak Mahindra Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, CSB Bank, and DCB Bank.  The acquisitions will be made as an investment manager for various mutual fund schemes.  This move provides ICICI Prudential AMC increased investment flexibility across its managed portfolios.
